extracted.intended_audience: health care providers, health IT developers, insurers/MA organizations, legal/regulatory commenters, and civil rights/compliance officers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and supporting citations from the HHS Section 1557 preamble concerning nondiscrimination, algorithmic decisionmaking, telehealth accessibility, privacy, and enforcement — intended to inform rulemaking comments, compliance, and implementation. Focuses on algorithm transparency, bias mitigation, telehealth accessibility, HIPAA/privacy, and enforcement processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individualized medical necessity determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: MA organizations must ensure that they are making medical necessity determinations based on the circumstances of the specific individual, as outlined at §422.101(c), as opposed to using an algorithm or software that doesn't account for an individual's circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited in CMS rulemaking (see 87 FR 22195): automated tools or algorithms used by Medicare Advantage organizations should not replace individualized determinations. Anti-pattern: relying on a one-size-fits-all algorithm that ignores patient-specific circumstances. Use-case: algorithms may inform workstreams but final determinations should reflect individual's clinical context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'intervention' in prediction/decision-support context
rubrics_metrics.description: ONC clarifies that the term 'intervention' in 'prediction decision support intervention' is not intended to mean a medical treatment but rather an intervention occurring within a workstream.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include alerts, order sets, flowsheets, dashboards, patient lists, documentation forms, relevant data presentations, protocol or pathway support, reference information or guidance, and reminder messages. Use this broader operational definition when classifying tools and applying program rules (ONC Final Rule, 89 FR 1192).

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of Crisis Standards of Care
rubrics_metrics.description: Crisis Standards of Care inform decision-making designed to accomplish the best outcome for a group of patients rather than focusing on an individual patient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a stated purpose/definition used in policy discussions; demonstrates that crisis standards prioritize population-level allocation decisions. Consider civil-rights implications when group-focused decisions may disproportionately affect protected groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithm transparency and information sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS/ONC and related Federal actions emphasize advancing health IT interoperability, algorithm transparency, and information sharing to address algorithmic risks and bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References include HHS Final Rule to advance Health IT interoperability and algorithm transparency, Guiding Principles to address potential bias, and related White House and agency fact sheets. Guidance implies requirements or expectations for documentation, explainability, provenance, and sharing of information about algorithms used in care.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIST AI RMF approach to tradeoffs and mitigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Where tradeoffs among trustworthy characteristics arise, measurement provides a traceable basis to inform management decisions; options may include recalibration, impact mitigation, or removal of the system from design, development, production, or use, as well as compensating, detective, deterrent, directive, and recovery controls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use measurement and traceability to justify management decisions about AI systems. When encountering fairness/performance tradeoffs, document rationale and select mitigations (e.g., recalibration, removal, controls). Cited from NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid proxy discrimination and inappropriate use of race/proxies
rubrics_metrics.description: Rulemaking and preamble discussion identify proxy discrimination (see §92.207) and provide examples where race-adjusted correction factors or other proxies produce disparate impacts on historically marginalized groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: race-adjusted correction factors in spirometry/nephrology/cardiology; Medicaid eligibility systems reducing benefits disproportionately; utilization algorithms using prior spending that under-represent Black patients. Anti-patterns include using race or close proxies without justification; recommended action is reassessment, transparency, and mitigation to prevent disparate impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize and address measurement/device bias (e.g., pulse oximetry)
rubrics_metrics.description: Empirical findings document racial and ethnic discrepancies in pulse oximetry and other measurement tools that can delay treatment eligibility or produce differential clinical outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite recent studies (NEJM, JAMA Intern Med.) and FDA safety communication on pulse oximeter accuracy; implication is to evaluate devices and clinical algorithms for measurement bias and correct or accommodate known limitations in clinical workflows and algorithm inputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governance and lifecycle management for clinical predictive models
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement governance frameworks that combine regulatory best practices and lifecycle management for predictive models used in clinical care, maintaining an active governance portfolio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors recommend oversight structures for local deployment of prediction models, active addition/removal and monitoring of models, and alignment with regulatory best practices (see Bedoya et al. and other governance frameworks). Governance should address monitoring, validation, updating, and documented decision processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telehealth nondiscrimination and accessibility obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal protections and guidance require nondiscrimination in telehealth to ensure accessibility for people with disabilities and persons with limited English proficiency (LEP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites OCR/DOJ guidance on nondiscrimination in telehealth (July 29, 2022), HRSA and HealthIT.gov resources on telehealth, and literature on addressing virtual care disparities. Implement accessibility features, language access, and reasonable modifications in telehealth services; anti-pattern: telehealth systems that are inaccessible to disabled or LEP patients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.1 (AA)
rubrics_metrics.description: WCAG 2.1 (AA) is cited as the accessibility standard for web content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use WCAG 2.1 AA conformance as a concrete standard for web and digital accessibility for health programs and information. This provides technical success criteria for accessibility (W3C Recommendation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect privacy and security of health information in telehealth and personal device contexts (HIPAA guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS OCR provides guidance on HIPAA Privacy Rule and disclosures relating to reproductive health care, protecting privacy/security when using personal cell phones or tablets, and how HIPAA permits audio-only telehealth under certain conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow OCR guidance documents on HIPAA privacy for reproductive health, mobile device communication, and audio-only telehealth. Operationalize safeguards for PHI on personal devices, use appropriate encryption/access controls when feasible, and document policies for telehealth communications to protect patient privacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide accessible complaint mechanisms and language support for civil rights enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR maintains filing processes and complaint portal and provides help in other languages and a Civil Rights/Conscience complaint form (with an expiration date listed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure affected individuals are informed about and can access OCR's complaint process (ocrportal.hhs.gov), provide language assistance, and make compliance-related information available. This supports enforcement and accountability for nondiscrimination obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reassess and justify clinical use of race in algorithms
rubrics_metrics.description: Calls to reconsider the use of race correction in clinical algorithms and to create databases tracking race-based clinical algorithms are cited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to NKF-ASN Task Force recommendations and recent literature urging reevaluation of race-based adjustments. Institutions should inventory algorithms that incorporate race, assess clinical justification, evaluate harms/benefits, and consider removing or modifying race-based inputs where inappropriate.
